original_question: Let T(n) = T112(3n+1, 3n+2), where T112(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that for every n >= 1 the quotient T(n) T(n+3) / (T(n+1) T(n+2)) equals 65536(2n+3)(2n+5)^2(2n+7)(4n+3)(4n+5)^2(4n+7)^2(4n+9)^2(4n+11) / (729(3n+2)(3n+4)^3(3n+5)^2(3n+7)^2(3n+8)^3(3n+10))?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 10 (both stones, two kinds of bones), concerning the central diagonal sequence T112(3n+1, 3n+2).
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's target almost exactly: it identifies the right sequence T(n) = T112(3n+1, 3n+2), correctly interprets T112 as allowing both stone orientations and exactly two bone orientations, states the same quotient T(n)T(n+3)/(T(n+1)T(n+2)), gives the exact rational product from the paper, and quantifies over n >= 1 exactly as in Problem 10.
missing_details: The draft is not fully stand-alone because it does not define the (a,b)-benzel region.
It should tie T112(a,b) explicitly to the paper's formal notation Tijk(a,b): right stone allowed iff i=1, left stone allowed iff j=1, and exactly k of the three bone prototiles allowed.
It should specify that tilings are by translates of the prototiles.
It should name the three bone orientations (vertical, rising, falling), or at least say that any fixed two of the three are allowed.
It should mention the symmetry fact used in the paper: for k=2, the count depends only on the number of allowed bone orientations, not on which orientation is forbidden.

For complete fidelity to the paper's setup, one can note that benzels are defined for integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a; for the specialization (a,b)=(3n+1,3n+2) with n >= 1 this condition is automatic.
refined_question: For integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be the union of unit hexagons whose barycentric-center coordinates (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfy i+j+k=1 and -(a-1) <= j-i, k-j, i-k <= b-1. Let T112(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel by translates of the right stone, the left stone, and any fixed two of the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, falling); equivalently, this is the paper's type-112 tiling number, and by threefold rotational symmetry it is independent of which bone orientation is excluded. If T(n) := T112(3n+1, 3n+2) for n >= 1, is it true that for every n >= 1 one has T(n)T(n+3)/(T(n+1)T(n+2)) = (65536*(2n+3)*(2n+5)^2*(2n+7)*(4n+3)*(4n+5)^2*(4n+7)^2*(4n+9)^2*(4n+11))/(729*(3n+2)*(3n+4)^3*(3n+5)^2*(3n+7)^2*(3n+8)^3*(3n+10))?
justification: This is the paper's Problem 10, stated in Section 7. The draft already reproduces the exact specialization T(n)=T112(3n+1,3n+2) and the precise quotient formula asked there. The only substantive omissions are the formal definition of the benzel and the paper's notation Tijk(a,b), together with the symmetry remark explaining why 'exactly two bone orientations are allowed' is well-defined without naming which one is forbidden. Nearby Problems 9, 11, 12, and 13 concern different diagonals or different sequences, so the sharp paper-faithful rewrite should stay exactly with Problem 10 rather than broadening to a larger family.

citations.label: definition of Tijk(a,b) and symmetry with respect to the number of allowed bone orientations
